html:
SMTO-LLM-0093 — The secure connection to your model service failed

GUID: 160c4f4a-2d8c-4b3a-8dfe-4bcdd397e6b2
Slug: llm-tls-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • SMTO started a secure connection to your model service, but it broke before a full answer came back. This isn't a certificate problem; the connection itself failed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and check the failing model's Endpoint. If the service isn't set up for encryption, the address should start with http://, not https://, and the other way round. Asking for a secure connection from a service that isn't set up for one is a common cause of this failure.
  2. Ask the person who runs the model service, or your network admin, to look at the service and any proxy in between for secure-connection errors at the time this happened. The error shows that the connection broke but not why; their logs show the cause.
  3. After the fix, select Check saved model on that model's card. It confirms a secure request now completes.
  4. Before asking SMTO to continue a task that stopped with this error, open its Conversation and check which steps it already finished. Steps finished before the error may already have made changes, and repeating them could do them twice.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model completes without a secure-connection error, and new tasks get answers from the model.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model service or your network. Don't turn off certificate or security checks to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An SSL/TLS protocol or handshake error (other than certificate verification) interrupted the connection to the model service before a complete response was received.

What this means

  • A TLS protocol or handshake error was reported. Certificate validation has its own category; this error alone does not identify a specific cipher, proxy or server defect.

Why this can happen

  • A TLS protocol or handshake error was reported. Certificate validation has its own category; this error alone does not identify a specific cipher, proxy or server defect.

How to diagnose it

  • The TLS connection failed before a complete model response was received.
  • The HTTPS request completes without a TLS error.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the base URL scheme matches the listener (https:// only against a TLS listener, http:// otherwise), then inspect TLS termination and any proxy logs at the failure time for handshake or protocol errors. Fix the transport issue without disabling verification, re-run Check saved model, and inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.
  • Check that the endpoint scheme and TLS listener agree. Ask the network/provider administrator to inspect TLS termination and proxy logs at the failure time. Correct the identified transport issue before submitting work again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • The HTTPS request completes without a TLS error.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
